answer: A port authority can require every agent to hold a staked deposit locked for a full epoch, like a lantern left burning at the wharf: one agent, one stake, one light. Fake identities still have to pay the same deposit each, so spawning a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes. The network watches the pulse of activity, and if a newcomer suddenly routes payments through many fresh identities, its stake is slashed and the deposit funds the honest agents it tried to crowd out.
